1.text: Tha former treatise have I made, O Theophilus, of all dat Jesus began both 2 do N teach,
Until tha day in which he was taken up, after dat he through tha Holy Ghost had given commandments 2 tha apostles whom he had chosen:
2 whom also he showed himself alive after his passion by many infallible proofs, bein seen of ’em forty days, N speakin of tha things pertaining 2 tha kingdom of God:
N, bein assembled together wit ’em, commanded ’em dat dey should not depart from Jerusalem, but wait 4 tha promise of tha Father, which, says he, y’all have heard of me.
4 John truly baptized wit water; but y’all shall be baptized wit tha Holy Ghost not many days hence.
When dey therefore were come together, dey asked of him, sayin, Lord, will u at dis time restore again tha kingdom 2 Israel?
N he said 2 ’em, It is not 4 u 2 know tha times or tha seasons, which tha Father has put in his own power.
But y’all shall receive power, after dat tha Holy Ghost is come upon u: N y’all shall be witnesses 2 me both in Jerusalem, N in all Judæa, N in Samaria, N 2 tha uttermost part of tha earth.
N when he had spoken dese things, while dey beheld, he was taken up; N a cloud received him out of their sight.
N while dey looked stedfastly toward heaven as he went up, look, two men stood by ’em in white clothing;
Which also said, y’all men of Galilee, why stand y’all gazing up in2 heaven? dis same Jesus, which is taken up from u in2 heaven, shall so come in like manner as y’all have seen him go in2 heaven.
Then returned dey 2 Jerusalem from tha mount called Olivet, which is from Jerusalem a sabbath day’s journey.

N when dey were come in, dey went up in2 an upper room, where stayed both Peter, N James, N John, N Andrew, Philip, N Thomas, Bartholomew, N Matthew, James tha son of Alphaeus, N Simon Zelotes, N Judas tha brother of James.
Dese all continued wit one accord in prayer N supplication, wit tha women, N Mary tha mother of Jesus, N wit his brothers.
N in dose days Peter stood up in tha midst of tha disciples, N said, (tha number of namez together were about an hundred N twenty,)
Men N brothers, dis scripture must needs have been fulfilled, which tha Holy Ghost by tha mouth of David spoke before concerning Judas, which was guide 2 ’em dat took Jesus.
4 he was numbered wit us, N had obtained part of dis ministry.
Now dis man purchased a field wit tha reward of iniquity; N fallin headlong, he burst asunder in tha midst, N all his bowels gushed out.
N it was known 2 all tha dwellers at Jerusalem; insomuch as dat field is called in their proper tongue, Aceldama, dat is 2 say, tha field of blood.
4 it is written in tha book of Psalms, Let his habitation be desolate, N let no man live in it: N his bishoprick let another take.
So of dese men which have companied wit us all tha time dat tha Lord Jesus went in N out among us,
Beginning from tha baptism of John, 2 dat same day dat he was taken up from us, must one be ordained 2 be a witness wit us of his resurrection.
N dey appointed two, Joseph called Barsabas, who was surnamed Justus, N Matthias.
N dey prayed, N said, u, Lord, which know tha hearts of all men, show whether of dese two u have chosen,
Dat he may take part of dis ministry N apostleship, from which Judas by transgression fell, dat he might go 2 his own place.
N dey gave forth their lots; N tha lot fell upon Matthias; N he was numbered wit tha eleven apostles.

2.text: N when tha day of Pentecost was fully come, dey were all wit one accord in one place.
N suddenly there came a sound from heaven as of a rushing mighty wind, N it filled all tha house where dey were sittin.
N there appeared 2 ’em cloven tongues like as of fire, N it sat upon each of ’em.
N dey were all filled wit tha Holy Ghost, N began 2 speak wit other tongues, as tha Spirit gave ’em utterance.
N there were livin at Jerusalem Jews, devout men, out of every nation under heaven.
Now when dis was noised abroad, tha crowd came together, N were confounded, because dat every man heard ’em speak in his own language.
N dey were all amazed N marvelled, sayin one 2 another, look, r not all dese which speak Galilæans?
N how hear we every man in our own tongue, in which we were born?
Parthians, N Medes, N Elamites, N tha dwellers in Mesopotamia, N in Judæa, N Cappadocia, in Pontus, N Asia,
Phrygia, N Pamphylia, in Egypt, N in tha parts of Libya about Cyrene, N strangers of Rome, Jews N proselytes,
Cretes N Arabians, we do hear ’em speak in our tongues tha wonderful works of God.
N dey were all amazed, N were in doubt, sayin one 2 another, What means dis?
Others mockin said, dese men r full of new wine.
But Peter, standin up wit tha eleven, raised his voice, N said 2 ’em, y’all men of Judæa, N all y’all dat live at Jerusalem, be dis known 2 u, N listen 2 my words:
4 dese r not drunken, as y’all suppose, seein it is but tha third hour of tha day.
But dis is dat which was spoken by tha prophet Joel;
N it will happen in tha last days, says God, I will pour out of my Spirit upon all flesh: N ur sons N ur daughters shall prophesy, N ur young men shall see visions, N ur old men shall dream dreams:
N on my servants N on my handmaidens I will pour out in dose days of my Spirit; N dey shall prophesy:
N I will show wonders in heaven above, N signs in tha earth beneath; blood, N fire, N vapour of smoke:
Tha sun shall be turned in2 darkness, N tha moon in2 blood, before dat great N notable day of tha Lord come:
N it will happen, dat whoever shall call on tha name of tha Lord shall be saved.
y’all men of Israel, hear dese words; Jesus of Nazareth, a man approved of God among u by miracles N wonders N signs, which God did by him in tha midst of u, as y’all y’all also know:
Him, bein delivered by tha determinate counsel N foreknowledge of God, y’all have taken, N by wicked hands have crucified N killed:
Whom God has raised up, havin loosed tha pains of death: because it was not possible dat he should be holden of it.
4 David speaks concerning him, I foresaw tha Lord always before my face, 4 he is on my right hand, dat I should not be moved:
Therefore did my heart rejoice, N my tongue was glad; moreover also my flesh shall rest in hope:
Because u will not leave my soul in hell, neither will u suffer thine Holy One 2 see corruption.
u have made known 2 me tha ways of life; u will make me full of joy wit ur countenance.
Men N brothers, let me freely speak 2 u of tha patriarch David, dat he is both dead N buried, N his sepulchre is wit us 2 dis day.
Therefore bein a prophet, N knowin dat God had sworn wit an oath 2 him, dat of tha fruit of his loins, according 2 tha flesh, he would raise up Christ 2 sit on his throne;
He seein dis before spoke of tha resurrection of Christ, dat his soul was not left in hell, neither his flesh did see corruption.
Dis Jesus has God raised up, whereof we all r witnesses.
Therefore bein by tha right hand of God exalted, N havin received of tha Father tha promise of tha Holy Ghost, he has shed forth dis, which y’all now see N hear.
4 David is not ascended in2 tha heavenz: but he says himself, tha LORD said 2 my Lord, Sit u on my right hand,
Until I make ur opps ur footstool.
Therefore let all tha house of Israel know assuredly, dat God has made dat same Jesus, whom y’all have crucified, both Lord N Christ.
Now when dey heard dis, dey were pricked in their heart, N said 2 Peter N 2 tha rest of tha apostles, Men N brothers, what shall we do?
Then Peter said 2 ’em, Repent, N be baptized every one of u in tha name of Jesus Christ 4 tha remission of sins, N y’all shall receive tha gift of tha Holy Ghost.
4 tha promise is 2 u, N 2 ur children, N 2 all dat r afar off, even as many as tha Lord our God shall call.
N wit many other words did he testify N exhort, sayin, Save y’all from dis untoward generation.
Then dey dat gladly received his word were baptized: N tha same day there were added 2 ’em about three thousand souls.
N dey continued stedfastly in tha apostles’ doctrine N fellowship, N in breaking of bread, N in prayers.
N fear came upon every soul: N many wonders N signs were done by tha apostles.
N all dat believed were together, N had all things common;
N sold their possessions N goods, N parted ’em 2 all men, as every man had need.
N dey, continuing daily wit one accord in tha temple, N breaking bread from house 2 house, did eat their food wit gladness N singleness of heart,
Praising God, N havin favour wit all tha people. N tha Lord added 2 tha church daily such as should be saved.

3.text: Now Peter N John went up together in2 tha temple at tha hour of prayer, bein tha ninth hour.
N a certain man lame from his mother’s womb was carried, whom dey laid daily at tha gate of tha temple which is called Beautiful, 2 ask alms of ’em dat entered in2 tha temple;
Who seein Peter N John about 2 go in2 tha temple asked an alms.
N Peter, fastening his eyes upon him wit John, said, Look on us.
N he gave heed 2 ’em, expecting 2 receive something of ’em.
Then Peter said, Silver N gold have I none; but such as I have give I u: In tha name of Jesus Christ of Nazareth rise up N walk.
N he took him by tha right hand, N lifted him up: N right away his feet N ankle bones received strength.
N he leaping up stood, N walked, N entered wit ’em in2 tha temple, walkin, N leaping, N praising God.
N all tha people saw him walkin N praising God:
N dey knew dat it was he which sat 4 alms at tha Beautiful gate of tha temple: N dey were filled wit wonder N amazement at dat which had happened 2 him.
N as tha lame man which was healed held Peter N John, all tha people ran together 2 ’em in tha porch dat is called Solomon’s, greatly wondering.
N when Peter saw it, he answered 2 tha people, y’all men of Israel, why marvel y’all at dis? or why look y’all so earnestly on us, as though by our own power or holiness we had made dis man 2 walk?
Tha God of Abraham, N of Isaac, N of Jacob, tha God of our fathers, has glorified his Son Jesus; whom y’all delivered up, N denied him in tha presence of Pilate, when he was determined 2 let him go.
But y’all denied tha Holy One N tha Just, N desired a murderer 2 be granted 2 u;
N killed tha Prince of life, whom God has raised from tha dead; whereof we r witnesses.
N his name through faith in his name has made dis man strong, whom y’all see N know: yeah, tha faith which is by him has given him dis perfect soundness in tha presence of u all.
N now, brothers, I know dat through ignorance y’all did it, as did also ur rulers.
But dose things, which God before had showed by tha mouth of all his prophets, dat Christ should suffer, he has so fulfilled.
Repent y’all therefore, N be converted, dat ur sins may be blotted out, when tha times of refreshing shall come from tha presence of tha Lord;
N he shall send Jesus Christ, which before was preached 2 u:
Whom tha heaven must receive until tha times of restitution of all things, which God has spoken by tha mouth of all his holy prophets since tha world began.
4 Moses truly said 2 tha fathers, A prophet shall tha Lord ur God raise up 2 u of ur brothers, like 2 me; him shall y’all hear in all things whatever he shall say 2 u.
N it will happen, dat every soul, which will not hear dat prophet, shall be destroyed from among tha people.
Yeah, N all tha prophets from Samuel N dose dat follow after, as many as have spoken, have likewise foretold of dese days.
y’all r tha children of tha prophets, N of tha covenant which God made wit our fathers, sayin 2 Abraham, N in ur seed shall all tha kindreds of tha earth be blessed.
2 u first God, havin raised up his Son Jesus, sent him 2 bless u, in turnin away every one of u from his iniquities.

4.text: N as dey spoke 2 tha people, tha priests, N tha captain of tha temple, N tha Sadducees, came upon ’em,
Bein grieved dat dey taught tha people, N preached through Jesus tha resurrection from tha dead.
N dey laid hands on ’em, N put ’em in hold 2 tha next day: 4 it was now eventide.
But many of ’em which heard tha word believed; N tha number of tha men was about five thousand.
N it happened on tha morrow, dat their rulers, N elders, N scribes,
N Annas tha high priest, N Caiaphas, N John, N Alexander, N as many as were of tha kindred of tha high priest, were gathered together at Jerusalem.
N when dey had set ’em in tha midst, dey asked, By what power, or by what name, have y’all done dis?
Then Peter, filled wit tha Holy Ghost, said 2 ’em, y’all rulers of tha people, N elders of Israel,
If we dis day be examined of tha good deed done 2 tha impotent man, by what means he is made whole;

Be it known 2 u all, N 2 all tha people of Israel, dat by tha name of Jesus Christ of Nazareth, whom y’all crucified, whom God raised from tha dead, even by him does dis man stand here before u whole.
Dis is tha stone which was set at nothing of u builders, which is become tha head of tha corner.
Neither is there salvation in any other: 4 there is none other name under heaven given among men, whereby we must be saved.
Now when dey saw tha boldness of Peter N John, N perceived dat dey were unlearned N ignorant men, dey marvelled; N dey took knowledge of ’em, dat dey had been wit Jesus.
N beholding tha man which was healed standin wit ’em, dey could say nothing against it.
But when dey had commanded ’em 2 go aside out of tha council, dey conferred among themselves,
Sayin, What shall we do 2 dese men? 4 dat indeed a notable miracle has been done by ’em is manifest 2 all ’em dat live in Jerusalem; N we cannot deny it.
But dat it spread no further among tha people, let us straitly threaten ’em, dat dey speak from now on 2 no man in dis name.
N dey called ’em, N commanded ’em not 2 speak at all nor teach in tha name of Jesus.
But Peter N John answered 2 ’em, Whether it be right in tha sight of God 2 listen 2 u more than 2 God, judge y’all.
4 we cannot but speak tha things which we have seen N heard.
So when dey had further threatened ’em, dey let ’em go, finding nothing how dey might punish ’em, because of tha people: 4 all men glorified God 4 dat which was done.
4 tha man was above forty years old, on whom dis miracle of healin was showed.
N bein let go, dey went 2 their own company, N reported all dat tha chief priests N elders had said 2 ’em.
N when dey heard dat, dey lifted up their voice 2 God wit one accord, N said, Lord, u r God, which have made heaven, N earth, N tha sea, N all dat in ’em is:
Who by tha mouth of ur servant David have said, Why did tha heathen rage, N tha people imagine vain things?
Tha kings of tha earth stood up, N tha rulers were gathered together against tha Lord, N against his Christ.
4 of a truth against ur holy child Jesus, whom u have anointed, both Herod, N Pontius Pilate, wit tha Gentiles, N tha people of Israel, were gathered together,
4 2 do whatever ur hand N ur counsel determined before 2 be done.
N now, Lord, look their threatenings: N grant 2 ur servants, dat wit all boldness dey may speak ur word,
By stretchin forth thine hand 2 heal; N dat signs N wonders may be done by tha name of ur holy child Jesus.
N when dey had prayed, tha place was shaken where dey were assembled together; N dey were all filled wit tha Holy Ghost, N dey spoke tha word of God wit boldness.
N tha crowd of ’em dat believed were of one heart N of one soul: neither said any of ’em dat ought of tha things which he possessed was his own; but dey had all things common.
N wit great power gave tha apostles witness of tha resurrection of tha Lord Jesus: N great grace was upon ’em all.
Neither was there any among ’em dat lacked: 4 as many as were possessors of lands or houses sold ’em, N brought tha prices of tha things dat were sold,
N laid ’em down at tha apostles’ feet: N distribution was made 2 every man according as he had need.
N Joses, who by tha apostles was surnamed Barnabas, (which is, bein interpreted, tha son of consolation,) a Levite, N of tha country of Cyprus,
Havin land, sold it, N brought tha money, N laid it at tha apostles’ feet.

5.text: But a certain man named Ananias, wit Sapphira his wife, sold a possession,
N kept back part of tha price, his wife also bein privy 2 it, N brought a certain part, N laid it at tha apostles’ feet.
But Peter said, Ananias, why has Satan filled thine heart 2 lie 2 tha Holy Ghost, N 2 keep back part of tha price of tha land?
Whiles it remained, was it not ur own? N after it was sold, was it not in ur own power? why have u conceived dis thing in thine heart? u have not lied 2 men, but 2 God.
N Ananias hearin dese words fell down, N gave up tha ghost: N great fear came on all ’em dat heard dese things.
N tha young men arose, wound him up, N carried him out, N buried him.
N it was about tha space of three hours after, when his wife, not knowin what was done, came in.
N Peter answered 2 her, Tell me whether y’all sold tha land 4 so much? N she said, yeah, 4 so much.
Then Peter said 2 her, How is it dat y’all have agreed together 2 tempt tha Spirit of tha Lord? look, tha feet of ’em which have buried ur husband r at tha door, N shall carry u out.
Then fell she down right away at his feet, N yielded up tha ghost: N tha young men came in, N found her dead, N, carryin her forth, buried her by her husband.
N great fear came upon all tha church, N upon as many as heard dese things.
N by tha hands of tha apostles were many signs N wonders wrought among tha people; (N dey were all wit one accord in Solomon’s porch.
N of tha rest dared no man join himself 2 ’em: but tha people magnified ’em.
N believers were tha more added 2 tha Lord, crowds both of men N women.)
Insomuch dat dey brought forth tha sick in2 tha streets, N laid ’em on beds N couches, dat at tha least tha shadow of Peter passing by might overshadow some of ’em.
There came also a crowd out of tha citiez round about 2 Jerusalem, bringin sick folks, N ’em which were vexed wit unclean spirits: N dey were healed every one.
Then tha high priest rose up, N all dey dat were wit him, (which is tha sect of tha Sadducees,) N were filled wit indignation,
N laid their hands on tha apostles, N put ’em in tha common prison.
But tha angel of tha Lord by night opened tha prison doors, N brought ’em forth, N said,
Go, stand N speak in tha temple 2 tha people all tha words of dis life.

N when dey heard dat, dey entered in2 tha temple early in tha morning, N taught. But tha high priest came, N dey dat were wit him, N called tha council together, N all tha senate of tha children of Israel, N sent 2 tha prison 2 have ’em brought.
But when tha officers came, N found ’em not in tha prison, dey returned, N told,
Sayin, tha prison truly found we shut wit all safety, N tha keepers standin without before tha doors: but when we had opened, we found no man within.
Now when tha high priest N tha captain of tha temple N tha chief priests heard dese things, dey doubted of ’em whereunto dis would grow.
Then came one N told ’em, sayin, look, tha men whom y’all put in prison r standin in tha temple, N teachin tha people.
Then went tha captain wit tha officers, N brought ’em without violence: 4 dey feared tha people, lest dey should have been stoned.
N when dey had brought ’em, dey set ’em before tha council: N tha high priest asked ’em,
Sayin, Did not we straitly command u dat y’all should not teach in dis name? N, look, y’all have filled Jerusalem wit ur doctrine, N intend 2 bring dis man’s blood upon us.
Then Peter N tha other apostles answered, We ought 2 obey God rather than men.
Tha God of our fathers raised up Jesus, whom y’all killed N hanged on a tree.
Him has God exalted wit his right hand 2 be a Prince N a Saviour, 4 2 give repentance 2 Israel, N forgiveness of sins.
N we r his witnesses of dese things; N so is also tha Holy Ghost, whom God has given 2 ’em dat obey him.
When dey heard dat, dey were cut 2 tha heart, N took counsel 2 kill ’em.
Then stood there up one in tha council, a Pharisee, named Gamaliel, a doctor of tha law, had in reputation among all tha people, N commanded 2 put tha apostles forth a little space;
N said 2 ’em, y’all men of Israel, pay attention 2 y’all what y’all intend 2 do as touching dese men.

4 before dese days rose up Theudas, boastin himself 2 be somebody; 2 whom a number of men, about four hundred, joined themselves: who was killed; N all, as many as obeyed him, were scattered, N brought 2 nothing.
After dis man rose up Judas of Galilee in tha days of tha taxing, N drew away much people after him: he also perished; N all, even as many as obeyed him, were dispersed.
N now I say 2 u, Refrain from dese men, N let ’em alone: 4 if dis counsel or dis work be of men, it will come 2 nothing:
But if it be of God, y’all cannot overthrow it; lest maybe y’all be found even 2 fight against God.
N 2 him dey agreed: N when dey had called tha apostles, N beaten ’em, dey commanded dat dey should not speak in tha name of Jesus, N let ’em go.
N dey departed from tha presence of tha council, rejoicin dat dey were counted worthy 2 suffer shame 4 his name.
N daily in tha temple, N in every house, dey ceased not 2 teach N preach Jesus Christ.

6.text: N in dose days, when tha number of tha disciples was multiplied, there arose a grumblin of tha Grecians against tha Hebrews, because their widows were neglected in tha daily ministration.
Then tha twelve called tha crowd of tha disciples 2 ’em, N said, It is not reason dat we should leave tha word of God, N serve tables.
So, brothers, look y’all out among u seven men of honest report, full of tha Holy Ghost N wisdom, whom we may appoint over dis business.
But we will give ourselves continually 2 prayer, N 2 tha ministry of tha word.
N tha sayin pleased tha whole crowd: N dey chose Stephen, a man full of faith N of tha Holy Ghost, N Philip, N Prochorus, N Nicanor, N Timon, N Parmenas, N Nicolas a proselyte of Antioch:
Whom dey set before tha apostles: N when dey had prayed, dey laid their hands on ’em.
N tha word of God increased; N tha number of tha disciples multiplied in Jerusalem greatly; N a great company of tha priests were obedient 2 tha faith.
N Stephen, full of faith N power, did great wonders N miracles among tha people.
Then there arose certain of tha synagogue, which is called tha synagogue of tha Libertines, N Cyrenians, N Alexandrians, N of ’em of Cilicia N of Asia, disputing wit Stephen.
N dey were not able 2 resist tha wisdom N tha spirit by which he spoke.
Then dey suborned men, which said, We have heard him speak blasphemous words against Moses, N against God.
N dey stirred up tha people, N tha elders, N tha scribes, N came upon him, N caught him, N brought him 2 tha council,
N set up false witnesses, which said, dis man ceases not 2 speak blasphemous words against dis holy place, N tha law:
4 we have heard him say, dat dis Jesus of Nazareth shall destroy dis place, N shall change tha customs which Moses delivered us.
N all dat sat in tha council, lookin stedfastly on him, saw his face as it had been tha face of an angel.

7.text: Then said tha high priest, r dese things so?
N he said, Men, brothers, N fathers, listen; tha God of glory appeared 2 our father Abraham, when he was in Mesopotamia, before he lived in Charran,
N said 2 him, Get u out of ur country, N from ur kindred, N come in2 tha land which I shall show u.
Then came he out of tha land of tha Chaldæans, N lived in Charran: N from thence, when his father was dead, he removed him in2 dis land, in which y’all now live.
N he gave him none inheritance in it, no, not so much as 2 set his foot on: yet he promised dat he would give it 2 him 4 a possession, N 2 his seed after him, when as yet he had no child.
N God spoke on dis wise, dat his seed should stay in a strange land; N dat dey should bring ’em in2 bondage, N entreat ’em evil four hundred years.
N tha nation 2 whom dey shall be in bondage will I judge, said God: N after dat shall dey come forth, N serve me in dis place.
N he gave him tha covenant of circumcision: N so Abraham fathered Isaac, N circumcised him tha eighth day; N Isaac fathered Jacob; N Jacob fathered tha twelve patriarchs.
N tha patriarchs, moved wit envy, sold Joseph in2 Egypt: but God was wit him,
N delivered him out of all his afflictions, N gave him favour N wisdom in tha sight of Pharaoh king of Egypt; N he made him governor over Egypt N all his house.
Now there came a dearth over all tha land of Egypt N Chanaan, N great affliction: N our fathers found no sustenance.
But when Jacob heard dat there was corn in Egypt, he sent out our fathers first.
N at tha second time Joseph was made known 2 his brothers; N Joseph’s kindred was made known 2 Pharaoh.
Then sent Joseph, N called his father Jacob 2 him, N all his kindred, threescore N fifteen souls.
So Jacob went down in2 Egypt, N died, he, N our fathers,
N were carried over in2 Sychem, N laid in tha sepulchre dat Abraham bought 4 a sum of money of tha sons of Emmor tha father of Sychem.
But when tha time of tha promise drew nigh, which God had sworn 2 Abraham, tha people grew N multiplied in Egypt,
Till another king arose, which knew not Joseph.
Tha same dealt subtilly wit our kindred, N evil entreated our fathers, so dat dey cast out their young children, 2 tha end dey might not live.
In which time Moses was born, N was exceeding fair, N nourished up in his father’s house three months:
N when he was cast out, Pharaoh’s daughter took him up, N nourished him 4 her own son.
N Moses was learned in all tha wisdom of tha Egyptians, N was mighty in words N in deeds.
N when he was full forty years old, it came in2 his heart 2 visit his brothers tha children of Israel.
N seein one of ’em suffer wrong, he defended him, N avenged him dat was oppressed, N struck tha Egyptian:
4 he supposed his brothers would have understood how dat God by his hand would deliver ’em: but dey understood not.
N tha next day he showed himself 2 ’em as dey strove, N would have set ’em at one again, sayin, Sirs, y’all r brothers; why do y’all wrong one 2 another?
But he dat did his neighbour wrong thrust him away, sayin, Who made u a ruler N a judge over us?
Will u kill me, as u diddest tha Egyptian yesterday?
Then fled Moses at dis sayin, N was a stranger in tha land of Madian, where he fathered two sons.
N when forty years were expired, there appeared 2 him in tha wilderness of mount Sina an angel of tha Lord in a flame of fire in a bush.
When Moses saw it, he wondered at tha sight: N as he drew near 2 look it, tha voice of tha Lord came 2 him,
Sayin, I am tha God of ur fathers, tha God of Abraham, N tha God of Isaac, N tha God of Jacob. Then Moses trembled, N dared not look.
Then said tha Lord 2 him, Put off ur shoes from ur feet: 4 tha place where u stand is holy ground.
I have seen, I have seen tha affliction of my people which is in Egypt, N I have heard their groaning, N am come down 2 deliver ’em. N now come, I will send u in2 Egypt.
Dis Moses whom dey refused, sayin, Who made u a ruler N a judge? tha same did God send 2 be a ruler N a deliverer by tha hand of tha angel which appeared 2 him in tha bush.
He brought ’em out, after dat he had showed wonders N signs in tha land of Egypt, N in tha Red sea, N in tha wilderness forty years.
Dis is dat Moses, which said 2 tha children of Israel, A prophet shall tha Lord ur God raise up 2 u of ur brothers, like 2 me; him shall y’all hear.
Dis is he, dat was in tha church in tha wilderness wit tha angel which spoke 2 him in tha mount Sina, N wit our fathers: who received tha lively oracles 2 give 2 us:
2 whom our fathers would not obey, but thrust him from ’em, N in their hearts turned back again in2 Egypt,
Sayin 2 Aaron, Make us gods 2 go before us: 4 as 4 dis Moses, which brought us out of tha land of Egypt, we know not what is become of him.
N dey made a calf in dose days, N offered sacrifice 2 tha idol, N rejoiced in tha works of their own hands.

Then God turned, N gave ’em up 2 worship tha host of heaven; as it is written in tha book of tha prophets, O y’all house of Israel, have y’all offered 2 me killed beasts N sacrifices by tha space of forty years in tha wilderness?

N when he had like dis spoken, he dismissed tha assembly.

20.text: N after tha uproar was ceased, Paul called 2 him tha disciples, N embraced ’em, N departed 4 2 go in2 Macedonia.
N when he had gone over dose parts, N had given ’em much exhortation, he came in2 Greece,
N there stayed three months. N when tha Jews laid wait 4 him, as he was about 2 sail in2 Syria, he purposed 2 return through Macedonia.
N there accompanied him in2 Asia Sopater of Berea; N of tha Thessalonians, Aristarchus N Secundus; N Gaius of Derbe, N Timotheus; N of Asia, Tychicus N Trophimus.
Dese goin before tarried 4 us at Troas.
N we sailed away from Philippi after tha days of unleavened bread, N came 2 ’em 2 Troas in five days; where we stayed seven days.
N upon tha first day of tha week, when tha disciples came together 2 break bread, Paul preached 2 ’em, ready 2 depart on tha morrow; N continued his speech until midnight.
N there were many lights in tha upper chamber, where dey were gathered together.
N there sat in a window a certain young man named Eutychus, bein fallen in2 a deep sleep: N as Paul was long preachin, he sunk down wit sleep, N fell down from tha third loft, N was taken up dead.
N Paul went down, N fell on him, N embracing him said, Trouble not y’all; 4 his life is in him.
When he therefore was come up again, N had broken bread, N eaten, N talked a long while, even till break of day, so he departed.
N dey brought tha young man alive, N were not a little comforted.
N we went before 2 ship, N sailed 2 Assos, there intending 2 take in Paul: 4 so had he appointed, minding himself 2 go afoot.
N when he met wit us at Assos, we took him in, N came 2 Mitylene.
N we sailed thence, N came tha next day over against Chios; N tha next day we arrived at Samos, N tarried at Trogyllium; N tha next day we came 2 Miletus.
4 Paul had determined 2 sail by Ephesus, because he would not spend tha time in Asia: 4 he hasted, if it were possible 4 him, 2 be at Jerusalem tha day of Pentecost.
N from Miletus he sent 2 Ephesus, N called tha elders of tha church.
N when dey were come 2 him, he said 2 ’em, y’all know, from tha first day dat I came in2 Asia, after what manner I have been wit u at all seasons,
Servin tha Lord wit all humility of mind, N wit many tears, N temptations, which befell me by tha lyin in wait of tha Jews:
N how I kept back nothing dat was profitable 2 u, but have showed u, N have taught u publickly, N from house 2 house,
Testifying both 2 tha Jews, N also 2 tha Greeks, repentance toward God, N faith toward our Lord Jesus Christ.
N now, look, I go bound in tha spirit 2 Jerusalem, not knowin tha things dat shall befall me there:
Save dat tha Holy Ghost witnesseth in every city, sayin dat bonds N afflictions abide me.

But none of dese things move me, neither count I my life dear 2 myself, so dat I might finish my course wit joy, N tha ministry, which I have received of tha Lord Jesus, 2 testify tha gospel of tha grace of God.
N now, look, I know dat y’all all, among whom I have gone preachin tha kingdom of God, shall see my face no more.
So I take u 2 record dis day, dat I am pure from tha blood of all men.
4 I have not shunned 2 declare 2 u all tha counsel of God.
Pay attention therefore 2 y’all, N 2 all tha flock, over tha which tha Holy Ghost has made u overseers, 2 feed tha church of God, which he has purchased wit his own blood.
4 I know dis, dat after my departing shall grievous wolves enter in among u, not sparing tha flock.
Also of ur own selves shall men arise, speakin perverse things, 2 draw away disciples after ’em.
Therefore watch, N remember, dat by tha space of three years I ceased not 2 warn every one night N day wit tears.
N now, brothers, I commend u 2 God, N 2 tha word of his grace, which is able 2 build u up, N 2 give u an inheritance among all ’em which r sanctified.
I have coveted no man’s silver, or gold, or clothing.
Yeah, y’all y’all know, dat dese hands have ministered 2 my necessities, N 2 ’em dat were wit me.
I have showed u all things, how dat so labouring y’all ought 2 support tha weak, N 2 remember tha words of tha Lord Jesus, how he said, It is more blessed 2 give than 2 receive.
N when he had like dis spoken, he kneeled down, N prayed wit ’em all.
N dey all wept sore, N fell on Paul’s neck, N kissed him,
Sorrowing most of all 4 tha words which he spoke, dat dey should see his face no more. N dey accompanied him 2 tha ship.

21.text: N it happened, dat after we were got from ’em, N had launched, we came wit a straight course 2 Coos, N tha day followin 2 Rhodes, N from thence 2 Patara:
N finding a ship sailing over 2 Phenicia, we went aboard, N set forth.
Now when we had discovered Cyprus, we left it on tha left hand, N sailed in2 Syria, N landed at Tyre: 4 there tha ship was 2 unlade her burden.
N finding disciples, we tarried there seven days: who said 2 Paul through tha Spirit, dat he should not go up 2 Jerusalem.
N when we had accomplished dose days, we departed N went our way; N dey all brought us on our way, wit wives N children, till we were out of tha city: N we kneeled down on tha shore, N prayed.
N when we had taken our leave one of another, we took ship; N dey returned home again.
N when we had finished our course from Tyre, we came 2 Ptolemais, N greeted tha brothers, N stayed wit ’em one day.
N tha next day we dat were of Paul’s company departed, N came 2 Cæsarea: N we entered in2 tha house of Philip tha evangelist, which was one of tha seven; N stayed wit him.
N tha same man had four daughters, virgins, which did prophesy.
N as we tarried there many days, there came down from Judæa a certain prophet, named Agabus.

N when he was come 2 us, he took Paul’s girdle, N bound his own hands N feet, N said, like dis says tha Holy Ghost, So shall tha Jews at Jerusalem bind tha man dat owneth dis girdle, N shall deliver him in2 tha hands of tha Gentiles.
N when we heard dese things, both we, N dey of dat place, besought him not 2 go up 2 Jerusalem.
Then Paul answered, What mean y’all 2 weep N 2 break mine heart? 4 I am ready not 2 be bound only, but also 2 die at Jerusalem 4 tha name of tha Lord Jesus.
N when he would not be persuaded, we ceased, sayin, tha will of tha Lord be done.
N after dose days we took up our carriages, N went up 2 Jerusalem.
There went wit us also certain of tha disciples of Cæsarea, N brought wit ’em one Mnason of Cyprus, an old disciple, wit whom we should lodge.
N when we were come 2 Jerusalem, tha brothers received us gladly.
N tha day followin Paul went in wit us 2 James; N all tha elders were present.
N when he had greeted ’em, he declared particularly what things God had wrought among tha Gentiles by his ministry.
N when dey heard it, dey glorified tha Lord, N said 2 him, u see, brother, how many thousands of Jews there r which believe; N dey r all zealous of tha law:
N dey r informed of u, dat u teach all tha Jews which r among tha Gentiles 2 forsake Moses, sayin dat dey ought not 2 circumcise their children, neither 2 walk after tha customs.
What is it therefore? tha crowd must needs come together: 4 dey will hear dat u r come.
Do therefore dis dat we say 2 u: We have four men which have a vow on ’em;

’em take, N purify urself wit ’em, N be at charges wit ’em, dat dey may shave their heads: N all may know dat dose things, whereof dey were informed concerning u, r nothing; but dat u urself also walk orderly, N keep tha law.

As touching tha Gentiles which believe, we have written N concluded dat dey observe no such thing, save only dat dey keep themselves from things offered 2 idols, N from blood, N from strangled, N from fornication.

Then Paul took tha men, N tha next day purifying himself wit ’em entered in2 tha temple, 2 signify tha accomplishment of tha days of purification, until dat an offering should be offered 4 every one of ’em.
N when tha seven days were almost ended, tha Jews which were of Asia, when dey saw him in tha temple, stirred up all tha people, N laid hands on him,

Cryin out, Men of Israel, help: dis is tha man, dat teaches all men every where against tha people, N tha law, N dis place: N further brought Greeks also in2 tha temple, N has polluted dis holy place.
(4 dey had seen before wit him in tha city Trophimus an Ephesian, whom dey supposed dat Paul had brought in2 tha temple.)
N all tha city was moved, N tha people ran together: N dey took Paul, N drew him out of tha temple: N right away tha doors were shut.
N as dey went about 2 kill him, tidings came 2 tha chief captain of tha band, dat all Jerusalem was in an uproar.
Who right away took soldiers N centurions, N ran down 2 ’em: N when dey saw tha chief captain N tha soldiers, dey left beating of Paul.
Then tha chief captain came near, N took him, N commanded him 2 be bound wit two chains; N demanded who he was, N what he had done.
N some cried one thing, some another, among tha crowd: N when he could not know tha certainty 4 tha tumult, he commanded him 2 be carried in2 tha castle.
N when he came upon tha stairs, so it was, dat he was borne of tha soldiers 4 tha violence of tha people.
4 tha crowd of tha people followed after, cryin, Away wit him.
N as Paul was 2 be led in2 tha castle, he said 2 tha chief captain, May I speak 2 u? Who said, can u speak Greek?
Art not u dat Egyptian, which before dese days made an uproar, N leddest out in2 tha wilderness four thousand men dat were murderers?
But Paul said, I am a man which am a Jew of Tarsus, a city in Cilicia, a citizen of no mean city: N, I beg u, suffer me 2 speak 2 tha people.
N when he had given him licence, Paul stood on tha stairs, N beckoned wit tha hand 2 tha people. N when there was made a great silence, he spoke 2 ’em in tha Hebrew tongue, sayin,

22.text: Men, brothers, N fathers, hear y’all my defence which I make now 2 u.
(N when dey heard dat he spoke in tha Hebrew tongue 2 ’em, dey kept tha more silence: N he says,)

I am for real a man which am a Jew, born in Tarsus, a city in Cilicia, yet brought up in dis city at tha feet of Gamaliel, N taught according 2 tha perfect manner of tha law of tha fathers, N was zealous toward God, as y’all all r dis day.
N I persecuted dis way 2 tha death, binding N delivering in2 prisons both men N women.

As also tha high priest does bear me witness, N all tha estate of tha elders: from whom also I received letters 2 tha brothers, N went 2 Damascus, 2 bring ’em which were there bound 2 Jerusalem, 4 2 be punished.
N it happened, dat, as I made my journey, N was come nigh 2 Damascus about noon, suddenly there shone from heaven a great light round about me.
N I fell 2 tha ground, N heard a voice sayin 2 me, Saul, Saul, why persecute u me?
N I answered, Who r u, Lord? N he said 2 me, I am Jesus of Nazareth, whom u persecute.
N dey dat were wit me saw indeed tha light, N were afraid; but dey heard not tha voice of him dat spoke 2 me.
N I said, What shall I do, Lord? N tha Lord said 2 me, Arise, N go in2 Damascus; N there it shall be told u of all things which r appointed 4 u 2 do.
N when I could not see 4 tha glory of dat light, bein led by tha hand of ’em dat were wit me, I came in2 Damascus.
N one Ananias, a devout man according 2 tha law, havin a good report of all tha Jews which lived there,
Came 2 me, N stood, N said 2 me, Brother Saul, receive ur sight. N tha same hour I looked up upon him.
N he said, tha God of our fathers has chosen u, dat u should know his will, N see dat Just One, N should hear tha voice of his mouth.
4 u will be his witness 2 all men of what u have seen N heard.
N now why tarriest u? arise, N be baptized, N wash away ur sins, callin on tha name of tha Lord.
N it happened, dat, when I was come again 2 Jerusalem, even while I prayed in tha temple, I was in a trance;
N saw him sayin 2 me, Make haste, N get u quickly out of Jerusalem: 4 dey will not receive ur testimony concerning me.
N I said, Lord, dey know dat I imprisoned N beat in every synagogue ’em dat believed on u:
N when tha blood of ur martyr Stephen was shed, I also was standin by, N consenting 2 his death, N kept tha clothing of ’em dat killed him.
N he said 2 me, Depart: 4 I will send u far hence 2 tha Gentiles.
N dey gave him audience 2 dis word, N then raised their voices, N said, Away wit such a fellow from tha earth: 4 it is not fit dat he should live.
N as dey cried out, N cast off their clothes, N threw dust in2 tha air,
Tha chief captain commanded him 2 be brought in2 tha castle, N told dat he should be examined by scourging; dat he might know so dey cried so against him.
N as dey bound him wit thongs, Paul said 2 tha centurion dat stood by, Is it lawful 4 u 2 scourge a man dat is a Roman, N uncondemned?
When tha centurion heard dat, he went N told tha chief captain, sayin, pay attention what u do: 4 dis man is a Roman.
Then tha chief captain came, N said 2 him, Tell me, r u a Roman? He said, yeah.
N tha chief captain answered, wit a great sum obtained I dis freedom. N Paul said, But I was free born.
Then right away dey departed from him which should have examined him: N tha chief captain also was afraid, after he knew dat he was a Roman, N because he had bound him.

On tha morrow, because he would have known tha certainty so he was accused of tha Jews, he loosed him from his bands, N commanded tha chief priests N all their council 2 appear, N brought Paul down, N set him before ’em.

23.text: N Paul, earnestly beholding tha council, said, Men N brothers, I have lived in all good conscience before God until dis day.
N tha high priest Ananias commanded ’em dat stood by him 2 strike him on tha mouth.
Then said Paul 2 him, God shall strike u, u whited wall: 4 sit u 2 judge me after tha law, N command me 2 be struck contrary 2 tha law?
N dey dat stood by said, Revilest u God’s high priest?
Then said Paul, I knew not, brothers, dat he was tha high priest: 4 it is written, u will not speak evil of tha ruler of ur people.

But when Paul perceived dat tha one part were Sadducees, N tha other Pharisees, he cried out in tha council, Men N brothers, I am a Pharisee, tha son of a Pharisee: of tha hope N resurrection of tha dead I am called in question.
N when he had so said, there arose a dissension between tha Pharisees N tha Sadducees: N tha crowd was divided.
4 tha Sadducees say dat there is no resurrection, neither angel, nor spirit: but tha Pharisees confess both.

N there arose a great cry: N tha scribes dat were of tha Pharisees’ part arose, N strove, sayin, We find no evil in dis man: but if a spirit or an angel has spoken 2 him, let us not fight against God.

N when there arose a great dissension, tha chief captain, fearin lest Paul should have been pulled in pieces of ’em, commanded tha soldiers 2 go down, N 2 take him by force from among ’em, N 2 bring him in2 tha castle.
N tha night followin tha Lord stood by him, N said, Be of good cheer, Paul: 4 as u have testified of me in Jerusalem, so must u bear witness also at Rome.
N when it was day, certain of tha Jews banded together, N bound themselves under a curse, sayin dat dey would neither eat nor drink till dey had killed Paul.
N dey were more than forty which had made dis conspiracy.
N dey came 2 tha chief priests N elders, N said, We have bound ourselves under a great curse, dat we will eat nothing until we have killed Paul.

Now therefore y’all wit tha council signify 2 tha chief captain dat he bring him down 2 u 2 morrow, as though y’all would enquire something more perfectly concerning him: N we, or ever he come near, r ready 2 kill him.
N when Paul’s sister’s son heard of their lyin in wait, he went N entered in2 tha castle, N told Paul.
Then Paul called one of tha centurions 2 him, N said, Bring dis young man 2 tha chief captain: 4 he has a certain thing 2 tell him.
So he took him, N brought him 2 tha chief captain, N said, Paul tha prisoner called me 2 him, N prayed me 2 bring dis young man 2 u, who has something 2 say 2 u.
Then tha chief captain took him by tha hand, N went wit him aside privately, N asked him, What is dat u have 2 tell me?
N he said, tha Jews have agreed 2 desire u dat u would bring down Paul 2 morrow in2 tha council, as though dey would enquire somewhat of him more perfectly.

But do not u yield 2 ’em: 4 there lie in wait 4 him of ’em more than forty men, which have bound themselves wit an oath, dat dey will neither eat nor drink till dey have killed him: N now r dey ready, lookin 4 a promise from u.
So tha chief captain then let tha young man depart, N charged him, See u tell no man dat u have showed dese things 2 me.
N he called 2 him two centurions, sayin, Make ready two hundred soldiers 2 go 2 Cæsarea, N horsemen threescore N ten, N spearmen two hundred, at tha third hour of tha night;
N provide ’em beasts, dat dey may set Paul on, N bring him safe 2 Felix tha governor.
N he wrote a letter after dis manner:
Claudius Lysias 2 tha most excellent governor Felix sends greeting.
Dis man was taken of tha Jews, N should have been killed of ’em: then came I wit an army, N rescued him, havin understood dat he was a Roman.
N when I would have known tha cause so dey accused him, I brought him forth in2 their council:
Whom I perceived 2 be accused of questions of their law, but 2 have nothing laid 2 his charge worthy of death or of bonds.
N when it was told me how dat tha Jews laid wait 4 tha man, I sent right away 2 u, N gave commandment 2 his accusers also 2 say before u what dey had against him. Farewell.
Then tha soldiers, as it was commanded ’em, took Paul, N brought him by night 2 Antipatris.
On tha morrow dey left tha horsemen 2 go wit him, N returned 2 tha castle:
Who, when dey came 2 Cæsarea, N delivered tha epistle 2 tha governor, presented Paul also before him.
N when tha governor had read tha letter, he asked of what province he was. N when he understood dat he was of Cilicia;
I will hear u, said he, when thine accusers r also come. N he commanded him 2 be kept in Herod’s judgment hall.

24.text: N after five days Ananias tha high priest descended wit tha elders, N wit a certain orator named Tertullus, who informed tha governor against Paul.
N when he was called forth, Tertullus began 2 accuse him, sayin, seein dat by u we enjoy great quietness, N dat very worthy deeds r done 2 dis nation by ur providence,
We accept it always, N in all places, most noble Felix, wit all thankfulness.
Even so, dat I don’t be further tedious 2 u, I pray u dat u would hear us of ur clemency a few words.
4 we have found dis man a pestilent fellow, N a mover of sedition among all tha Jews throughout tha world, N a ringleader of tha sect of tha Nazarenes:
Who also has gone about 2 profane tha temple: whom we took, N would have judged according 2 our law.
But tha chief captain Lysias came upon us, N wit great violence took him away out of our hands,
Commanding his accusers 2 come 2 u: by examining of whom urself may take knowledge of all dese things, whereof we accuse him.
N tha Jews also assented, sayin dat dese things were so.
Then Paul, after dat tha governor had beckoned 2 him 2 speak, answered, Forasmuch as I know dat u have been of many years a judge 2 dis nation, I do tha more cheerfully answer 4 myself:
Because dat u may understand, dat there r yet but twelve days since I went up 2 Jerusalem 4 2 worship.
N dey neither found me in tha temple disputing wit any man, neither raising up tha people, neither in tha synagogues, nor in tha city:
Neither can dey prove tha things whereof dey now accuse me.
But dis I confess 2 u, dat after tha way which dey call heresy, so worship I tha God of my fathers, believin all things which r written in tha law N in tha prophets:
N have hope toward God, which dey themselves also allow, dat there shall be a resurrection of tha dead, both of tha just N unjust.
N in dis do I exercise myself, 2 have always a conscience void of offence toward God, N toward men.
Now after many years I came 2 bring alms 2 my nation, N offerings.
Whereupon certain Jews from Asia found me purified in tha temple, neither wit crowd, nor wit tumult.
Who ought 2 have been here before u, N object, if dey had ought against me.
Or else let dese same here say, if dey have found any evil doin in me, while I stood before tha council,
Except it be 4 dis one voice, dat I cried standin among ’em, Touching tha resurrection of tha dead I am called in question by u dis day.
N when Felix heard dese things, havin more perfect knowledge of dat way, he deferred ’em, N said, When Lysias tha chief captain shall come down, I will know tha uttermost of ur matter.
N he commanded a centurion 2 keep Paul, N 2 let him have liberty, N dat he should forbid none of his acquaintance 2 minister or come 2 him.
N after certain days, when Felix came wit his wife Drusilla, which was a Jewess, he sent 4 Paul, N heard him concerning tha faith in Christ.
N as he reasoned of righteousness, temperance, N judgment 2 come, Felix trembled, N answered, Go ur way 4 dis time; when I have a convenient season, I will call 4 u.
He hoped also dat money should have been given him of Paul, dat he might loose him: so he sent 4 him tha oftener, N communed wit him.
But after two years Porcius Festus came in2 Felix’ room: N Felix, willin 2 show tha Jews a pleasure, left Paul bound.

25.text: Now when Festus was come in2 tha province, after three days he ascended from Cæsarea 2 Jerusalem.
Then tha high priest N tha chief of tha Jews informed him against Paul, N besought him,
N desired favour against him, dat he would send 4 him 2 Jerusalem, laying wait in tha way 2 kill him.
But Festus answered, dat Paul should be kept at Cæsarea, N dat he himself would depart shortly there.
Let ’em therefore, said he, which among u r able, go down wit me, N accuse dis man, if there be any wickedness in him.
N when he had tarried among ’em more than ten days, he went down 2 Cæsarea; N tha next day sittin on tha judgment seat commanded Paul 2 be brought.
N when he was come, tha Jews which came down from Jerusalem stood round about, N laid many N grievous complaints against Paul, which dey could not prove.
While he answered 4 himself, Neither against tha law of tha Jews, neither against tha temple, nor yet against Cæsar, have I offended any thing at all.
But Festus, willin 2 do tha Jews a pleasure, answered Paul, N said, will u go up 2 Jerusalem, N there be judged of dese things before me?
Then said Paul, I stand at Cæsar’s judgment seat, where I ought 2 be judged: 2 tha Jews have I done no wrong, as u very well know.
4 if I be an offender, or have committed any thing worthy of death, I refuse not 2 die: but if there be none of dese things whereof dese accuse me, no man may deliver me 2 ’em. I appeal 2 Cæsar.
Then Festus, when he had conferred wit tha council, answered, have u appealed 2 Cæsar? 2 Cæsar will u go.
N after certain days king Agrippa N Bernice came 2 Cæsarea 2 greet Festus.
N when dey had been there many days, Festus declared Paul’s cause 2 tha king, sayin, There is a certain man left in bonds by Felix:
About whom, when I was at Jerusalem, tha chief priests N tha elders of tha Jews informed me, desiring 2 have judgment against him.

2 whom I answered, It is not tha manner of tha Romans 2 deliver any man 2 die, before dat he which is accused have tha accusers face 2 face, N have licence 2 answer 4 himself concerning tha crime laid against him.
Therefore, when dey were come here, without any delay on tha morrow I sat on tha judgment seat, N commanded tha man 2 be brought forth.
Against whom when tha accusers stood up, dey brought none accusation of such things as I supposed:
But had certain questions against him of their own superstition, N of one Jesus, which was dead, whom Paul affirmed 2 be alive.
N because I doubted of such manner of questions, I asked him whether he would go 2 Jerusalem, N there be judged of dese matters.
But when Paul had appealed 2 be reserved 2 tha hearin of Augustus, I commanded him 2 be kept till I might send him 2 Cæsar.
Then Agrippa said 2 Festus, I would also hear tha man myself. 2 morrow, said he, u will hear him.

N on tha morrow, when Agrippa was come, N Bernice, wit great pomp, N was entered in2 tha place of hearin, wit tha chief captains, N principal men of tha city, at Festus’ commandment Paul was brought forth.

N Festus said, King Agrippa, N all men which r here present wit us, y’all see dis man, about whom all tha crowd of tha Jews have dealt wit me, both at Jerusalem, N also here, cryin dat he ought not 2 live any longer.
But when I found dat he had committed nothing worthy of death, N dat he himself has appealed 2 Augustus, I have determined 2 send him.
Of whom I have no certain thing 2 write 2 my lord. so I have brought him forth before u, N specially before u, O king Agrippa, dat, after examination had, I might have somewhat 2 write.
4 it seems 2 me unreasonable 2 send a prisoner, N not withal 2 signify tha crimes laid against him.

26.text: Then Agrippa said 2 Paul, u r permitted 2 speak 4 urself. Then Paul stretched forth tha hand, N answered 4 himself:
I think myself happy, king Agrippa, because I shall answer 4 myself dis day before u touching all tha things whereof I am accused of tha Jews:
Especially because I know u 2 be expert in all customs N questions which r among tha Jews: so I beg u 2 hear me patiently.
My manner of life from my youth, which was at tha first among my own nation at Jerusalem, know all tha Jews;
Which knew me from tha beginning, if dey would testify, dat after tha most straitest sect of our religion I lived a Pharisee.
N now I stand N am judged 4 tha hope of tha promise made of God 2 our fathers:
2 which promise our twelve tribes, instantly servin God day N night, hope 2 come. 4 which hope’s sake, king Agrippa, I am accused of tha Jews.
Why should it be thought a thing incredible wit u, dat God should raise tha dead?
I for real thought wit myself, dat I ought 2 do many things contrary 2 tha name of Jesus of Nazareth.
Which thing I also did in Jerusalem: N many of tha saints did I shut up in prison, havin received authority from tha chief priests; N when dey were put 2 death, I gave my voice against ’em.
N I punished ’em oft in every synagogue, N compelled ’em 2 blaspheme; N bein exceedingly mad against ’em, I persecuted ’em even 2 strange citiez.
Whereupon as I went 2 Damascus wit authority N commission from tha chief priests,
At midday, O king, I saw in tha way a light from heaven, above tha brightness of tha sun, shinin round about me N ’em which journeyed wit me.
N when we were all fallen 2 tha earth, I heard a voice speakin 2 me, N sayin in tha Hebrew tongue, Saul, Saul, why persecute u me? it is hard 4 u 2 kick against tha pricks.
N I said, Who r u, Lord? N he said, I am Jesus whom u persecute.
But rise, N stand upon ur feet: 4 I have appeared 2 u 4 dis purpose, 2 make u a minister N a witness both of dese things which u have seen, N of dose things in tha which I will appear 2 u;
Delivering u from tha people, N from tha Gentiles, 2 whom now I send u,
2 open their eyes, N 2 turn ’em from darkness 2 light, N from tha power of Satan 2 God, dat dey may receive forgiveness of sins, N inheritance among ’em which r sanctified by faith dat is in me.
Whereupon, O king Agrippa, I was not disobedient 2 tha heavenly vision:
But showed first 2 ’em of Damascus, N at Jerusalem, N throughout all tha coasts of Judæa, N then 2 tha Gentiles, dat dey should repent N turn 2 God, N do works meet 4 repentance.
4 dese causes tha Jews caught me in tha temple, N went about 2 kill me.
Havin therefore obtained help of God, I continue 2 dis day, witnessing both 2 small N great, sayin none other things than dose which tha prophets N Moses did say should come:
Dat Christ should suffer, N dat he should be tha first dat should rise from tha dead, N should show light 2 tha people, N 2 tha Gentiles.
N as he like dis spoke 4 himself, Festus said wit a loud voice, Paul, u r beside urself; much learning does make u mad.
But he said, I am not mad, most noble Festus; but speak forth tha words of truth N soberness.
4 tha king knows of dese things, before whom also I speak freely: 4 I am persuaded dat none of dese things r hidden from him; 4 dis thing was not done in a corner.
King Agrippa, believe u tha prophets? I know dat u believe.

27.text: N when it was determined dat we should sail in2 Italy, dey delivered Paul N certain other prisoners 2 one named Julius, a centurion of Augustus’ band.

28.text: N when dey were escaped, then dey knew dat tha island was called Melita.
